utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-97-25-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milorad Kronjelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference which is being held simply to comply with the Rules. Appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: If it please the Court. For the Prosecution, Dirk Ryneveld, and with me today are Daryl Mundis and our case manager, George Huber. We're prepared to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. For the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on behalf of the Defence, legal counsel Miroslav Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, you are filling in for Mr. Bakrac, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, now, the amended indictment seems to have got past without a further hitch. Where does the Prosecution stand, Mr. Ryneveld?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Our view was that -- my initial reading of Rule 72 was such that the material, if my friend was going to make any further preliminary motions, it would have been within 30 days after our amended indictment was accepted for filing by the Registry on the 3rd of March. We took the view that since those 30 days had passed and we had not received any notice in writing, that the matter was a foregone conclusion. Nevertheless, at a very brief meeting in my office this morning with the Defence, I understand that my friend may actually have an application to make orally before the Court. So that's what I'm advising the Court at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's see what it's all about. Mr. Vasic, what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the position of the Defence differs from the position of the Prosecution. Namely, it is our view that in accordance with Article 21 of the Statute and Rule 50(C), 52 -- no, I'm sorry, 53(B) and 47(G), the deadline for a preliminary motion begins on the day he received the amended indictment in the language he knows, and that was the 30th of March, 2000. Therefore, it is the Defence intention to submit a preliminary motion regarding the form of the indictment, though we realise that the amended indictment has now been further specified, and our preliminary motion would consist of only two or three points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think there is a problem with the way in which you've interpreted the Statute and the Rules, but I know that in previous cases the Trial Chambers have usually taken the view that you should have 30 days from the day you receive the amended indictment in a language which the accused understands. You say that was the 30th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 30th of March, 2000. That is when the Defence received the amended indictment in a language the accused understands, and the accused has just told me that he received that indictment around the 3rd or 4th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. But you received it on the 30th of March?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, in a language the accused understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think the time will run from then. You say that you only have a few matters to raise this time. They better be new ones, if I may put it as baldly as I can, because on the previous occasion Mr. Bakrac tried to rerun a few issues that had already been determined against him. If you have now decided that there are just these few points to be raised, when can you get your motion on?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Bakrac is currently in Belgrade. He's finalising the motion, and we hope that the motion will reach the Tribunal in the course of this week, not later than the 15th [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you'll need a date, you see, and I'm only trying to work out when a suitable period might be, subject to what the Prosecution might say. So you think it will be here within the week?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by the end of the week at the latest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. I made a mistake with the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Ryneveld, that has indeed been the previous experience. I'm not sure about the translation, but it seems only fair that they should be able to read it. If I give the 30-day extension as from the 30th of March, would that be any problem from the Prosecution's point of view?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No, it ought not to. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Does that mean that nothing has been done yet about interviewing the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Apart from further discussions indicating as to when that might take place, we have had those further discussions, including discussions about stipulations, however everything seems to depend on the finalisation of the form of the final amended indictment. So to answer your question directly, apart from talking that we ought to do this some day, it is depending on the finalisation of the amended indictment, so yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm not sure why, if I might say so. Anyway --

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: Well, I can only say that we're anxious to do it now. However --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, you can only do it by consent, so that will be the end of that. Very well. Then I'll make an order extending the time within which a preliminary motion may be filed as to the form of the amended indictment until the 30th of April. Now, Mr. Vasic, I think at that stage you better start talking a little bit more closely with the Prosecution. I can understand your desire or your client's desire to know precisely the case he has to meet, but there are limits to this, and if, as I suspect, these points must be very small ones indeed, the time has come for the case to start moving forward. You are the next case in the list to be heard, and whilst I have no promises to make, it may be that you will be on in a reasonably foreseeable future, so that there is a lot of work to be done in the meantime. Would you convey those comments to Mr. Bakrac so that the matter will proceed as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to thank you for your comments. In our conversations with the Prosecution, we have roughly fixed certain dates, whether it may be May or June, but most probably June, when we could have the accused interviewed, and we could also discuss stipulations, so that the Defence will join in the efforts to speed up things as much as possible. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That sounds very much more promising, and I'm grateful to you for that. Are there any other matters, Mr. Ryneveld, in relation to the preparation that you want to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. RYNEVELD
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour. I believe those are all the matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Vasic, are there any other matters within the terms of the Rule 65 bis, the Status Conference Rule, that you want to raise on behalf of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much, but I have no other points to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right then. We'll leave the Status Conference there. Hopefully at the next Status Conference we'll be able to get forward more than we have so far. I will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: adjourned at 10.10 a.m.
